headline: Why Le Pen's plan for a constitutional referendum would be 'a coup d'état in form and content'
description: If she were to win, far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen has pledged to call a referendum to revise the Constitution and enshrine the far right's core principles in it. According to a member of the highest administrative court, this would be 'a double coup d'état, both in form and content.'

headline: French government tries to defuse victims' anger over wildfires
description: Despite announcing emergency measures, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu faced angry victims in Gironde on Monday. In the Var, President Emmanuel Macron stressed the technical aspects of firefighting, but avoided mention of climate change.

headline: Jean Hegland, American novelist: 'The idea that humans must dominate the Earth and animals has not served us well'
description: In an interview with Le Monde, the author of the cult novel 'Into the Forest' calls for thinking beyond infinite growth, which she sees as incompatible with protecting the living world.

headline: Tiananmen Square massacre: Le Monde reveals unseen footage of the Chinese regime's violent repression
description: Art historian Nathalie Trouveroy shared footage with Le Monde from her personal archives of the Tiananmen Square protests, shedding new light on how the Chinese regime violently repressed the student protests in June 1989.
